_: Worsted wool suiting (2/2 twill or plain, ~230-280 g/m2), finished; conditioned 20 C 65 % RH. No single measured KES set for a named worsted was retrieved: the values are the magnitudes of Kawabata's men's-suiting population (recalled) and are marked E. Wool is the reference fabric for KES, so a measured fabric should replace these first.

alpha.src: matte, scaly fibres with a light nap; no BRDF fit retrieved

n.src: E: recalled from Morton & Hearle 2008 (MORTON08), not re-read: MORTON08 mean

sheen.v: low; worsted twill shows a faint diagonal ridge highlight

fibre_n.src: E: recalled from Morton & Hearle 2008 (MORTON08), not re-read: MORTON08 wool 1.553 / 1.542 (recalled; the brief says 1.55)

wet_darkening.src: LEKNER88 / Angstrom film model, diffuse light; the index-matching effect inside the yarn (ZHANG06) darkens further and is not in this formula; white thin fabric also turns translucent (fibre/water index ratio ~1.16 instead of ~1.55 in air)

static.src: E: recalled from Morton & Hearle 2008 (MORTON08), not re-read: fabric-on-fabric 0.2-0.6 band (search summaries); wool's scales give a directional difference (against-scale higher, MORTON08 recalled)

kes_MIU.src: E: recalled from Kawabata 1980 (KAWABATA80), not re-read: KAWABATA80 suiting population magnitude (recalled)

surface_energy_mJ_m2.src: hydrophobic 18-MEA lipid surface (WOOLWET advancing 103 deg implies a low polar part); value not retrieved

water_contact_angle_deg.src: WOOLWET single-fibre Wilhelmy, hair as wool's model; the surface repels liquid water while the core absorbs vapour

moisture_regain_pct.src: ASTMD1909 (worsted tops; ~16 % for some wool classes is E: recalled, not re-read)

water_absorption.src: E: recalled from Morton & Hearle 2008 (MORTON08), not re-read: wool's high vapour uptake (MORTON08, recalled); liquid uptake of a finished suiting is slow at first (hydrophobic surface)

triboelectric.src: ALPHALAB wool 0 nC/J on its scale (zero = mean conductor), still positive against polyester; ordinal series place wool positive

surface_resistivity_ohm_sq.src: E: recalled from Morton & Hearle 2008 (MORTON08), not re-read: wool sits ~1-2 decades above cotton at the same RH (MORTON08, recalled)

felting.v: wet + agitation + heat: irreversible shrink (directional scale friction)
felting.src: E: recalled from Morton & Hearle 2008 (MORTON08), not re-read: MORTON08 (recalled)

collision_thickness_mm.src: half of T0 0.62 mm at 0.5 gf/cm2 (KAWABATA80 suiting magnitudes, recalled (LC ~0.37, RC ~50 %); inputs E)

contact_stiffness_kPa_per_mm.src: KES-FB3 secant: (4.903 - 0.049) kPa / (T0 0.62 - Tm 0.42) mm (KAWABATA80 suiting magnitudes, recalled (LC ~0.37, RC ~50 %); inputs E)

initial_stiffness_kPa_per_mm.src: secant x LC 0.37: LC < 1 means the pile is soft first then stiffens as fibres pack

compressible_to_fraction.src: Tm / T0 at 50 gf/cm2 (~5 kPa, a firm press or sitting); beyond it the fibres themselves resist (fibre modulus, GPa)

penetration_response.ramp_note: stiffening ramp (LC < 1): IPC log barrier starting at collision_thickness, or a two-slope ramp initial -> secant

contact_damping_ratio.src: (1 - RC 50 %) / (4 pi): energy lost per press-release cycle; RC from KAWABATA80 suiting magnitudes, recalled (LC ~0.37, RC ~50 %)

restitution.src: a cloth layer dropped or slapped on a rigid flat does not bounce: energy goes into bending and fibre friction (no measurement found)

response_time_ms.src: a cloth flap / slap reads as a short damped crack; set by the in-plane wave crossing a ~0.3 m panel at the speeds below plus bending

wave_speed_m_s.src: sqrt(stretch_N_m 10896 / mass 0.25 kg/m2) and sqrt(shear_N_m_rad 42.1 / mass); transverse (flutter) speed is sqrt(tension / mass) and depends on load

min_separation_mm.src: two half-thicknesses: folded layers rest T0 apart at light pressure, Tm under ~5 kPa

fibre_density_kg_m3.src: E: recalled from Morton & Hearle 2008 (MORTON08), not re-read: MORTON08 wool 1.31 g/cm3 (recalled)

areal_density_g_m2.src: E: recalled from Kawabata 1980 (KAWABATA80), not re-read: KAWABATA80 winter suiting W ~24-25 mg/cm2 (recalled); summer 180-220

bending_rigidity_gfcm2_cm.src: E: recalled from Kawabata 1980 (KAWABATA80), not re-read: KAWABATA80 suiting ~0.08-0.12 (recalled)

bending_hysteresis_2HB_gfcm_cm.src: E: recalled from Kawabata 1980 (KAWABATA80), not re-read: KAWABATA80 (recalled)

poisson.src: Penava group measured wool plain weave (2017), numbers not retrieved

recovery.v: good: creases fall out after hanging, faster in steam
recovery.src: E: recalled from Morton & Hearle 2008 (MORTON08), not re-read: high RT and fibre crimp (MORTON08, recalled)

sim._: Per unit width / area; for a triangle mesh with edge length h, spring k_edge ~ k_membrane (square cells) and XPBD compliance alpha = 1/k. Secant to the KES maximum load: the real curve is soft-then-stiff (toe region), so use these as the stiff branch and ~1/3 of it below 1 % strain unless a curve is fitted

bend_compliance_1_per_Nm.src: 1 / bend (N m per unit width); a dihedral constraint's compliance scales with edge length / area of the hinge

shear_N_m_rad.src: UNITS G x 56.19 from KES guide G 0.75 (E)

bending_length_cm.src: c = (B / W)^(1/3), B gf cm2/cm, W gf/cm2 (Peirce cantilever relation): the cantilever check a sim should reproduce

heat_capacity_J_kgK.src: E: recalled from Morton & Hearle 2008 (MORTON08), not re-read: MORTON08 (recalled)

wet.src: E: recalled from Morton & Hearle 2008 (MORTON08), not re-read: KIM85: wool fabric bending rigidity RISES slightly with water and its bending hysteresis rises steeply up to the fibre's maximum regain (direction M, size E ~+10 %); the fibre itself softens (wet modulus roughly a third of dry, MORTON08 recalled) and loses ~10-20 % strength; mass doubles soaked (E)

steamed.src: hot-wet wool sets into a new shape (permanent set); recovery of creases is fastest here

ASTMD1909.cite: ASTM D1909-13(2020)e1 Standard tables of commercial moisture regains for textile fibres (cotton 8.5, wool 13.6, silk 11, flax 12, nylon 4.5, polyester 0.4 %); read through a CC BY review table citing it (Bioresour Bioprocess 2020, 10.1186/s40643-020-00339-1 Table 10) and the ASTM catalogue abstracts. Commercial (agreed) regains, close to equilibrium at 65 % RH, 21 C
ASTMD1909.lic: paywalled standard; the numbers are facts

KIM85.cite: Kim S-G. Effect of water on the bending properties of wool, polyester and wool-polyester blended fabrics. Textile Science and Engineering (Korea) 22(3):43-52 (1985). Abstract only: bending rigidity of wool and blends rises slightly with water content; polyester falls; bending hysteresis of wool rises steeply up to wool's maximum regain then levels
KIM85.lic: abstract read; full text not opened; direction of the effect used

WOOLWET.cite: J Cosmet Sci 61(2) (2010), single-fibre Wilhelmy wetting of wool / human hair as its model (library.scconline.org v061n02): scoured fibre advancing ~103 deg; removing 18-MEA: advancing 103 -> 88, receding 60 -> 3 deg (search summary)

LEKNER88.cite: Lekner J, Dorf MC. Why some things are darker when wet. Appl Opt 27(7):1278-1280 (1988): a water film's total internal reflection returns diffuse light to an absorbing surface for another chance of absorption (Angstrom), plus a lower relative index inside
LEKNER88.lic: paywalled journal; author copy; formula used, text studied only

ZHANG06.cite: Zhang H, Voss KJ. Bidirectional reflectance study on dry, wet and submerged particulate layers: effects of pore liquid refractive index and translucent particle concentrations. Appl Opt 45 (2006): index matching lets light go deeper and be absorbed; neither model alone sufficient
ZHANG06.lic: paywalled journal; author copy; studied only

SANAD16.cite: Sanad RA, Cassidy T. Fabric objective measurement and drape. Textile Progress 47(4):317-406 (2016): Cusick drape, 18 cm disc / 30 cm sample gives DC 30-98 % from limp to stiff; specimen 24 cm when DC < 30 %, 36 cm when > 85 %
SANAD16.lic: accepted version, all rights reserved; studied, ranges used as facts

MORTON08.cite: Morton WE, Hearle JWS. Physical Properties of Textile Fibres, 4th ed. Woodhead (2008): fibre densities, refractive indices, moduli, wet/dry strength, electrical resistance. Recalled; not re-opened in this session
MORTON08.lic: copyrighted book; individual numbers as facts; recalled, so marked E

KAWABATA80.cite: Kawabata S. The Standardization and Analysis of Hand Evaluation, 2nd ed. Textile Machinery Society of Japan (1980): KES-FB conditions (tensile max 500 gf/cm, shear to 8 deg, bending to K = +/-2.5 cm-1) and the men's suiting populations. Recalled, not re-opened
KAWABATA80.lic: copyrighted book; conditions and typical magnitudes recalled, marked E

ALPHALAB.cite: AlphaLab Inc. (W. Lee) triboelectric table, charge affinity nC/J at ~22 C, 35 % RH (2009); cotton +5, wool 0 read from secondary copies (blog / Scribd); nylon listed with dry skin at +30
ALPHALAB.lic: (c) AlphaLab, may be reproduced only whole; single numbers used as facts, table not copied

UNITS.cite: Unit conversions done here: 1 gf = 9.80665 mN; KES B gf cm2/cm x 98.07 = uN m per unit width; KES G gf/(cm deg) x 56.19 = N/m per rad; KES-FB1 standard max load 500 gf/cm = 490.3 N/m; 1 oz/yd2 = 33.906 g/m2; 1 momme = 4.306 g/m2; 1 ft3/ft2/min (ASTM D737, 125 Pa) = 5.08 mm/s

TYPICAL.cite: Trade and textbook typical values (fabric weight classes, Martindale rating bands such as EN 14465 upholstery 'heavy domestic' >= 25 000 rubs, fabric emissivity ~0.9, effective fabric conductivity dominated by trapped air 0.03-0.06 W/mK). Used only where no measured value was retrieved; each use says why
